name: Lighting Conditions
description: Variations in ambient light (sunlight, shadows, cloud cover) significantly impact the clarity and contrast of images, making human analysis more time-consuming when images are poorly lit and more straightforward when images are well lit.  This is the most likely factor due to its constant and ubiquitous influence.

name: Weather Conditions
description: Rain, fog, snow, and haze dramatically degrade image quality, increasing the difficulty for both human operators and the onboard classifier. Severe weather would likely trigger a higher proportion of failed analyses and longer human review times.

name: Object Orientation/Pose
description: The angle at which objects appear in the images (e.g., a person facing sideways vs. directly) affects how easily a human operator can identify them, and how effectively a classifier can interpret features.  Complex poses often require more cognitive effort.

name: Target Visibility/Obscuration
description: Partial obstructions to the target (e.g., vegetation, buildings) make it harder for both humans and the classifier to discern the object's features, leading to more analysis time.

name: UAV Movement/Stabilization
description: Movement of the UAV during image capture can introduce blur and distortions.  This is more pronounced at higher altitudes or with turbulent air.  The impact varies with image classifier robustness to motion.

name: Operator Fatigue/Experience
description: Human operator attention and analysis speed can fluctuate throughout the mission due to fatigue or variations in experience.  This will create a distribution of processing times.

name: Onboard Classifier Confidence Threshold
description: The threshold at which the classifier triggers a ‘failed’ analysis can impact the volume of images sent to the human operator. A higher threshold might lead to more ‘failed’ classifications and, consequently, increased review time.

name: Image Resolution/Sensor Quality
description: Lower resolution or poorer sensor quality leads to less detailed images, making identification more difficult for both humans and the classifier.

name: Time of Day/Sun Angle
description: Sun angle and shadows shift throughout the day, affecting lighting conditions and the visibility of objects. This has a strong correlation with lighting conditions.

name: Target Size/Distance
description: Smaller or more distant targets require higher resolution images and potentially more complex processing (either human or automated) to identify them.

name: Terrain Features
description: The specific terrain features (e.g., forests, urban areas, water bodies) influence both the image content and the difficulty of visual analysis. Forests, for example, are often more difficult for human and automated vision systems.

name: System Latency
description: Latency between image capture, transmission to the operator, and human/classifier processing adds variability to the overall time.

name: Operational Mode (e.g., Autonomous vs. Assisted)
description: The level of human intervention (e.g., proactive requests for images versus reactive review) can impact the observed processing times.  A more reactive approach will naturally introduce variability.

name: UAV Navigation Accuracy
description: Inaccurate positioning can cause the UAV to capture images slightly off-target or at suboptimal angles, impacting the relevance of the images and thus the time taken to process.

name: Image Compression Settings
description: Higher compression leads to lower quality images, increasing the difficulty for both human operators and the classifier.
